A thunderous cavalry charge smashing headlong into a braced spear-wall, lances shattering, horses rearing, the front rank exploding into chaos and dust.
Two great front lines colliding in a single deafening crash of steel and shields, the impact rippling down the ranks, men and beasts buckling.
A desperate last stand — a shrinking ring of battered defenders back-to-back, hemmed in on all sides by a closing enemy tide.
Siege ladders swarming a high wall, screaming attackers clambering over bodies, defenders heaving stones, the parapet drowning in smoke and flailing limbs.
A shield-wall buckling inward under a savage charge, the center bowing, men stumbling, the formation cracking apart like splintering timber.
A breakthrough punching clean through the enemy center, riders flooding the gap, the opposing line folding left and right in sudden collapse.
A routed army breaking and fleeing in blind terror, pursued men hurling down shields, the field dissolving into screaming, scattered, stumbling chaos.
A furious clash at a breached gate, defenders and attackers locked chest-to-chest in smoke-choked rubble, iron ringing against iron without pause.
A flanking ambush erupting from dense woodland, hitting the enemy rear like a hammer, their formation convulsing inward with shock and screaming confusion.
Massed infantry grinding in deep melee, neither line yielding, men pushing shield-to-shield, the dead trampled beneath boots as pressure builds ceaselessly.
A counter-charge surging out from a crumbling flank, fresh soldiers smashing into exhausted attackers, momentum reversing, the entire battle line suddenly pivoting.
A war elephant crashing through a pikemen formation, soldiers scattering like scattered kindling, trumpeting madly, its armored flanks slick with blood.
Catapult stones arcing down into massed ranks, each impact detonating in a crater of shattered bodies, the formation rippling outward in panic.
A narrow bridge fight — two packed columns ramming each other above dark rushing water, men pitched screaming over the railings below.
Mounted archers sweeping along an exposed flank, loosing in fluid motion, iron-tipped volleys tearing through unshielded infantry unable to close the distance.
A night assault erupting from total darkness, torchlight suddenly blazing, defenders scrambling half-armored, the camp dissolving into frantic desperate close-quarters slaughter.
A river crossing under fire — wading soldiers struggling through current, arrows thudding into water, men dragged under by armor and crashing comrades.
Two cavalry columns colliding head-on at full gallop, a catastrophic tangle of horses and lances, the impact hurling riders skyward in arcs.
A defender pouring boiling oil down a siege ladder, men shrieking and falling, the assault faltering, the ladder swinging loose against the wall.
A phalanx advancing in lockstep, overlapping shields lowered, sarissas leveled outward like a bristling moving wall grinding everything before it into retreat.
An exhausted breakthrough force cut off deep in enemy territory, surrounded now, forming a desperate circle, shields interlocked, fighting outward in all directions.
A berserker charge — a wedge of screaming warriors hurling themselves without formation into a disciplined line, sheer ferocious impact buckling the spearmen backward.
Grappling hooks biting the top of a siege tower, defenders hauling ropes, the tower tilting, groaning, then crashing sideways into the ditch below.
A reserve column unleashed at the critical instant, hammering into an already-strained flank, the sheer fresh weight shattering cohesion like a dropped blade.
The final gate giving way with a deafening crack, a tide of attackers flooding inward, the last defenders swallowed by the surging iron wave.
